newsitem.title: ITALY: Pilot critically injured in Italy plane accident.
newsitem.headline: Pilot critically injured in Italy plane accident.

text.p: At least five people were injured, one critically, when a small airliner overshot a runway at Florence airport on Wednesday and stopped just short of a busy highway, police and doctors said.
The pilot of the France-based Air Littoral ATR-42 turbo prop plane was in a coma at a Florence hospital, doctors said. They had not yet decided whether to operate.
The names and nationalities of the two pilots, one hostess and 14 passengers were not immediately available.

The plane, on a flight from the French resort of Nice, failed to stop at the end of the runway after landing at the small Florence airport, which is equipped only for visual and not instrument landings.

It broke through a perimeter fence and ploughed on towards a motorway, its nose hitting the highway guard rail. Television footage showed parts of the 23-metre-long (74 foot) plane had been snapped off.
Firemen cut into the wreckage to free the pilots but the passengers left the plane by a rear door.
Doctors said at least five passengers were injured but none seriously. All of the passengers had been taken to hospitals for checks but most were expected to be released during the day.
The highway, a major east-west link which leads to Italy's Mediterranean coast, was closed and traffic was backed up for several kilometres (miles).
Magistrates began an investigation into the accident and police said the plane's flight recorder had been recovered.
The airport handles national and European flights and is situated near the Tuscan capital. A larger airport further away from Florence serves intercontinental traffic.
Air Littoral, a French regional airline which is majority-owned by businessman Michel Seydoux, is based in Montpellier, France.
